newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FORECAST - Dutch June CPI seen rising 2.4 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Dutch June CPI seen rising 2.4 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Dutch economists expect Dutch June consumer price inflation to show a 2.4 percent rise year-on-year, compared with a 2.2 percent rise in May.
The figure will be released on Friday, July 11, at 0830 GMT.
Analysts agreed the beginning of summer sales was likely to have dampened inflation, but they were split over the development of food prices in June.

MeesPierson said the beginning of summer sales and lower fruit and vegetables prices were likely to have dampened month-on-month inflation, adding the main part of May's rise in coffee and pork meat prices was a thing of the past.

Generale Bank and Rabobank pointed at the usual drop in the monthly figure at this time of the year - due to the beginning of summer clothing and shoes sales - but added this was partly offset by higher food prices.
NIB Securities mentioned gradually declining meat prices.
Forecasts contributed by: ABN AMRO, Generale Bank, ING, MeesPierson, J.P. Morgan, NIB Securities, Rabobank.
